lōrīca, lōrīcae f.

noun, first declension

a cuirass, a breastplate

First a leather corselet, then any cuirass, even one of linen (Suet. Galb. 19; Lewis & Short); also a breastwork on a rampart (Caes. BG 5.39). De Vaan lists it among the derivatives of lōrum, a thong, while reporting that some take it for a loan word.

Other words

  • thōrāx, thōrācis m. — a breastplate

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 4.20.7; Verg. A. 10.337 (Lewis & Short)

    Greek θώραξ, the chest, and so the armour over it; rarer than lōrīca.

Examples

  • prō lōrīcā malacum capiam pallium

    instead of a breastplate I’ll take a soft cloakPlaut. Bacch. 1.1.37 (Lewis & Short)

See also helmet, shield, sword, soldier.
